findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct AC-10 to say the passing line carries all FOUR keys (environment/principal/privilege_posture/instrument), matching the four-field contract in Approach 1a.
evidence: AC: 'a `provenance:` continuation line indented under an `[operator-attested]` item, carrying all three keys, binds to that item and passes'
Approach 1a: 'FOUR key=value pairs separated by ;, keys exactly environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument'
1a: 'Why instrument is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have'
findings.finding: AC-10 (the declaration-syntax AC) says the passing continuation line carries 'all three keys', but the contract defined in the Approach (section 1a) requires FOUR fields — environment, principal, privilege_posture, AND instrument — with instrument explicitly called out as the escape-2b-critical fourth field. The AC undercounts the contract it is meant to pin end to end.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'a test pins the DECLARATION SYNTAX end to end' AC; contrast with Approach 1a ('FOUR key=value pairs')
scenarios: An implementer writes the syntax-binding test against a three-key line, so a declaration missing `instrument` binds-and-passes — exactly re-opening escape 2b the story exists to close.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'carrying all three keys' to 'carrying all four keys' in the declaration-syntax AC, and include `instrument` in the passing-fixture line.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the DET check requires the post-em-dash justification to be present and non-placeholder, and add an AC/test for it.
evidence: 1a Form rule: 'the justification follows an em-dash' — but the placeholder-rejection paragraph and the DET-owns bullet enumerate only the four values and the two enums, never the justification text
'The DET check ... owns: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder values, and membership of the two enum fields' — justification not mentioned
findings.finding: The DET check's placeholder/presence rules are specified for the four key=value VALUES and the two enum literal sets, but nothing states whether the one-line justification that must follow the em-dash is itself checked for presence/non-placeholder. An author can write a valid four-key line with an empty or 'TBD' justification and it is unclear whether the deterministic check flags it.
findings.location: Approach 1a ('the justification follows an em-dash'; 'Placeholder rejection') and the DET-check ownership bullet
scenarios: A declaration 'environment=X; principal=Y; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — TBD' — is the empty/placeholder justification a finding or not? The plan does not say.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to 1a's placeholder-rejection rules and the DET-owns bullet: the justification text after the em-dash MUST be present and non-placeholder (same placeholder set); add a unit-tier test asserting an empty/TBD justification is flagged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the `justification` (em-dash tail) to a component: either require the DET presence/non-placeholder check to cover it, or state explicitly in the rubric that a missing/vacuous justification is (or is not) a finding — so no element of the declaration is left mechanism-less
evidence: Canonical form shows `... instrument=<...> — <one-line justification>` and the 'Form' rule says 'the justification follows an em-dash'
privilege_posture is defined as 'one of ... plus a one-line justification of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out'
DET ownership: 'presence of all four keys, non-placeholder values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets' — justification not listed

AGENT ownership: rules '(a) environment-vs-repo-anchor, (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization judgement' — none reads the justification
The 'Placeholder rejection' rule enumerates the four key=value pairs; the justification is not a keyed field, so its placeholder/absence handling is unspecified
findings.finding: The `justification` element of the provenance declaration (the trailing em-dash text in the canonical form, and the 'one-line justification of why that posture can exhibit the failure' in the privilege_posture definition) is part of the structured contract the LLM criterion consumes, but no component is assigned to check its presence or judge its content: the DET-ownership bullet lists only the four keys + non-placeholder + enum membership, and AGENT rules (a)-(d) judge environment/no-anchor/posture-literal/instrument — the justification is in neither, so an executor has no rule for a missing, empty, or vacuous justification.
findings.location: Section 'Approach' item 1a (canonical form + 'Form' rule) and 'Which component produces which judgement'
scenarios: An author writes `... privilege_posture=broader — TBD` (or omits the em-dash tail entirely); the DET check passes (four keys present, enums valid) and no AGENT rule fires, so the posture claim ships with no stated justification — the exact 'recorded assertion someone can challenge' the plan promises is empty
Two implementers disagree on whether a missing justification is a DET presence failure or an AGENT finding, because the ownership split never assigns it
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the DET check's presence+non-placeholder assertion to the justification text (treat empty / TBD / N/A after the em-dash as absent), OR add a rule to the rubric that a missing or placeholder justification on a declared posture is a finding; pick one and record it in the component-ownership split.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a prior-art note to the Approach/ADR: state whether the `environment`/`principal`/`privilege_posture`/`instrument` schema deliberately follows or diverges from SLSA/in-toto provenance semantics AND from the in-repo DSSE/in-toto attestation substrate (ADR-0044, `src/rebar/attest/`), whose HMAC scheme already targets the 'produced in this environment / not transplanted' problem.
evidence: Plan §1: 'declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp: environment ... principal ... privilege_posture ... instrument' — a provenance schema over an attestation.

Retrieved SLSA/in-toto: 'A SLSA provenance attestation ... contains: the builder identity ... the source repository URL and commit SHA, the build trigger ... build parameters' — the same WHERE/WHO/WHAT-produced-it shape the plan invents from scratch.

ADR-0044 (in-repo): 'Reuse established standards rather than hand-roll crypto ... DSSE is the Sigstore / in-toto / SLSA standard'; the HMAC substrate 'proves a verdict was produced *in this environment* and hasn't been transplanted' — the wrong-environment problem this plan re-solves at the text layer without cross-referencing.
The plan cites ADR-0043 and ADR-0054 but nowhere considers SLSA/in-toto provenance or ADR-0044 / src/rebar/attest as prior art for the schema (ABSENCE).
findings.finding: The plan introduces a NOVEL attestation-provenance schema (`environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` / `instrument`) — capturing where, under whose identity, and with what kind of instrument a measurement was produced — without considering directly-analogous, well-established prior art. The four fields mirror almost one-for-one the SLSA provenance predicate / in-toto attestation model (builder identity, invocation environment, materials, what-was-executed). More strikingly, THIS repo already ships a DSSE/in-toto/SLSA-based attestation substrate (ADR-0044, `src/rebar/attest/`) whose stated design principle is 'reuse established standards rather than hand-roll' and whose HMAC scheme exists precisely to prove a verdict 'was produced *in this environment* and hasn't been transplanted' — the exact wrong-environment escape this plan targets. The plan's prior-art reasoning engages only its own ADR-0043 attestation lineage and never asks whether the provenance-schema design should adopt (or explicitly diverge from) SLSA/in-toto provenance semantics or the in-repo attest substrate.
findings.location: Approach §1 (measurement-provenance fields) and §1a (declaration form); Scope 'Concrete names pinned'
scenarios: The schema is finalized ad hoc; a later story discovers the field names/semantics should have aligned with the in-repo attest substrate or SLSA predicate keys, forcing a contract migration the plan claims to avoid.
Reviewers/consumers cannot tell whether divergence from the established provenance vocabulary (builder/invocation/environment) is deliberate or an oversight.
findings.suggested_fix: In the new ADR (and Approach §1), add a short 'Prior art' paragraph: cite SLSA provenance / in-toto attestation as the established shape for 'attest the environment + identity + invocation that produced an artifact', and cite ADR-0044 / src/rebar/attest as the in-repo standards-based substrate whose per-environment HMAC already addresses transplant/wrong-environment; justify why this story uses free-text provenance fields on the ticket rather than reusing/aligning with those (e.g., the escape lives in plan-time review text the completion attestation never covers), so the divergence is a recorded decision rather than an omission.

findings.finding: AC-5's instrument-vs-authorization judgement (flag instrument=simulation on an AUTHORIZATION claim even at privilege_posture=production-equivalent; pass instrument=live-call) has NO mechanism assigned to produce it, so the epic's self-described sharpest escape (2b) stays uncaught.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC-5 (instrument field); cross-checked against Approach §2 and Scope's rubric decision-rules list
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fourth rubric decision rule: '(d) a criterion verifying an authorization/permission claim while declaring instrument=simulation or instrument=static-analysis is a finding, regardless of privilege_posture, because a simulator/static check is not interchangeable with a live call for an authorization claim; instrument=live-call is not flagged.' Keep the DET check presence-only (omitted instrument -> absent) and move the semantic judgement to the LLM rubric where the escape-2b probe belongs.

findings.finding: AC-5's `instrument`-vs-authorization decision rule — flag `instrument=simulation` on a criterion making an AUTHORIZATION claim even when `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, and pass `instrument=live-call` — is referenced but not co-located in the rubric prompt spec, which is pinned to exactly three decision rules that omit it. Neither the presence-only DET check (which explicitly 'makes no judgement about whether they are right') nor the three enumerated rubric rules can produce this finding, so no specified mechanism emits AC-5's required output.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC-5; cross-checked against Scope (`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` rubric spec, 'must state the three decision rules in one place') and Approach S2
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope entry for `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md`, extend 'must state the three decision rules' to FOUR and add: '(d) `instrument: simulation` or `static-analysis` on a criterion making an authorization/permission claim — a finding, even at `privilege_posture: production-equivalent`; `instrument: live-call` — no finding.' Confirm AC-5 maps this judgment to the AGENT criterion, not the DET presence check.

findings.finding: The stated rationale for pinning exec:AGENT ('At 1-TURN it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run') misattributes the tooling grant, and the cited precedent for AGENT+trigger routing (project.engine-layer-enforcement) is actually exec:1-TURN, not AGENT.

The contract enumerates THREE fields in Approach step 1 and in the AC-1 deterministic-check text (environment / principal / privilege_posture), but Section 1a and a dedicated AC make `instrument` a REQUIRED FOURTH field checked by the same deterministic presence check. Approach-1 and AC-1 under-enumerate the required field set relative to Section 1a's canonical form (FOUR key=value pairs).
findings.location: Approach step 1; Section 1a; first Acceptance Criterion
findings.suggested_fix: Amend Approach step 1 to add `instrument` as the fourth declared field, and amend AC-1 to read 'lacking environment / principal / privilege_posture / instrument'.
